cands.name: Kathy Castor
cands.bio: Democratic U.S. Representative since 2007 (District 11, then 14). Land-use attorney; Hillsborough County commissioner 2002-2006; chaired the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis 2019-2023. Ranking member of the Energy and Commerce Energy subcommittee. Daughter of Betty Castor.
cands.local_ties: Born in Miami, raised and lives in Tampa. The new District 14 lies entirely within Hillsborough County; the map removed the old cross-bay link to St. Petersburg (WUSF).

record.text: Committees (119th Congress): Energy and Commerce (ranking member, Energy subcommittee) and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the U.S. and the Chinese Communist Party.

2025: proposed legislation to bar power companies from using ratepayer revenue for lobbying and campaign donations. Sept. 2026: voted for a House resolution denouncing socialism and the Democratic Socialists of America (per Wikipedia).
Called the May 2026 Florida map 'blatantly unconstitutional' but committed to running for re-election.

money_notes.text: Endorsed by AIPAC, EMILY's List, League of Conservation Voters Action Fund, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Sierra Club, Giffords, AFGE, Florida AFL-CIO and UAW (per Wikipedia's 2026 election page).

cands.name: Mike Beltran
cands.bio: Republican nominee; attorney (Penn B.A. 2005, Harvard J.D. 2008). Florida House member 2018-2024 (District 57, then District 70 after redistricting). Won an eight-way Aug. 18 GOP primary with 45.6%. Calls himself 'MAGA Mike.'
cands.local_ties: Practiced law in the Tampa Bay area; his former House seat was in Hillsborough County. New District 14 lies entirely within Hillsborough County (WUSF). Residence not stated in sources reviewed.

record.text: Sponsored bills allowing graduating high-school students to wear armed-forces uniforms at commencement (signed 2019), restricting minors' indoor vaping, and a safe-haven infant surrender law; offered a 2023 amendment to allow open carry that failed (per Wikipedia).
Fox 13 interview (Oct. 8, 2026): said he would vote to end federal sugar price supports, opposes cutting National Flood Insurance Program benefits but would favor income-based premium adjustments.

money_notes.text: Endorsed by Club for Growth PAC (Aug. 31, 2026) and the Freedom Caucus Fund (Aug. 19, 2026), per Wikipedia citing those organizations.

Oct. 29, 2026: Beltran's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist to Building Together PAC, the Castor campaign and the DCCC over text messages saying he takes 'campaign cash from health insurance, tech, and Wall Street companies' while serving on oversight committees; his lawyers called the claim 'plainly and knowingly defamatory' and noted he left the Florida House in 2024.

Tampa Bay Times reports the National Republican Congressional Committee is targeting four Florida seats made more Republican-leaning by redistricting; its headline says the national GOP elevated Beltran.

controversies.text: Sept. 1, 2026: the Washington Examiner reported he removed prominent mentions of Donald Trump (and earlier criticism of Gov. DeSantis) from his campaign website after winning the primary; no campaign explanation was reported.
Oct. 2026 dispute with Building Together PAC over text messages about his campaign contributions (see money notes); his lawyers call the claims defamatory.

endorsements.text: Reps. Gus Bilirakis and Greg Steube; former state Sen. Jeff Brandes; Florida House leaders Tyler Sirois and Wyman Duggan; former Senate President Tom Lee; Gun Owners of America; Republican Liberty Caucus; Club for Growth PAC; Freedom Caucus Fund (per Wikipedia).
